title: The small pro-etale site of a weakly etale X-scheme is the localization of X_proet
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme, $A$ a commutative ring, and let $j:W\to X$ be a weakly etale morphism with $W$ an object of the small pro-etale site $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] (for instance an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion] of an open subscheme $W\subset X$). Then: (1) for every object $V\to W$ of $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ the composite $V\to W\to X$ is weakly etale, and $\iota_j:(V\to W)\mapsto(V\to W\to X,\ V\to W)$ is a canonical equivalence of categories (an isomorphism on the concrete bounded-object categories before choosing small skeleta) from $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ onto the localization $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/W$ [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] (an $X$-morphism $V\to W$ from an object $V\to X$ of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ is weakly etale because $V\to X$ and $W\to X$ are), under which the coverings of $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ are exactly the coverings of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/W$; so $\iota_j$ identifies the two sites and their categories of sheaves. (2) Under $\iota_j$ the restriction $A_X|_W$, $(A_X|_W)(V\to W)=A_X(V\to X)$, of the constant sheaf of rings $A_X$ [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] is identified with the constant sheaf of rings $A_W$ on $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$, by the unique map of sheaves of rings $A_W\to A_X|_W$ that is the identity on the constant sections $a\in A$, which is an isomorphism. (3) Consequently restriction $F\mapsto F|_W$, $F|_W(V\to W)=F(V\to X)$, is a functor $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\to\Sh(W_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and sheaves of $A_W$-modules on $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$ are the same as sheaves of $A_X|_W$-modules on $X_{\mathrm{proet}}/W$. (4) If $j$ is an open immersion then $j$ is a monomorphism, so every object $V\to X$ of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ has at most one $X$-morphism to $W$, and it has one exactly when $V\to X$ factors through the open subscheme $W$ (set-theoretically, when its image lies in $W$).

proof.text: Work with the same bounded schemes in the universes of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and first with concrete objects rather than independently chosen skeleta [def-weil-size-convention]. By [lem-weil-pbc-weakly-etale-composition-base-change], $V\to W$ weakly etale implies $V\to X$ weakly etale. Conversely an object $(V\to X,a:V\to W)$ of the slice satisfies $j\circ a=V\to X$, and [lem-trf-weakly-etale-between-objects] applied over $X$ shows that $a$ is weakly etale, since both $V\to X$ and $W\to X$ are weakly etale. These assignments preserve the underlying scheme and arrow, and are inverse on objects. A morphism on either side is exactly a scheme map $b:V\to V^{\prime}$ with $a^{\prime}\circ b=a$; this also gives its required triangle over $X$. They are therefore inverse on morphisms and preserve identity and composition. Passing to small skeleta gives the stated canonical equivalence, rather than an equality of independently chosen object sets.

By [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], a covering of an object $V\to W$ is a family of weakly etale arrows $V_i\to V$ satisfying the fpqc finite-affine-cover condition on every affine open of $V$. This condition mentions only those arrows and their images in $V$, not the ultimate base $W$ or $X$. In the slice the underlying objects are the same schemes by step 1, and by [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] the covering families are exactly their coverings over $X$. Hence both sites have precisely the same covering families. Precomposition with the inverse assignments sends the sheaf matching/gluing condition to the identical condition; applying these precompositions successively gives the identity. This explicitly identifies the sheaf categories (up to the skeleton equivalences), proving the rest of (1).

Put $\mathcal C=X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and let $P$ be the constant ring presheaf with value $A$. Its restriction to $\mathcal C/W$ is again the constant ring presheaf with identity transition maps. By [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], $P^\#=A_X$, and by step 2 the sheafification of $P|_W$ is $A_W$. Apply [lem-pur-ring-presheaf-sheafification-localization] to $P$ and $W$: its ring-sheaf isomorphism is $A_W\to A_X|_W$, and its unit identity says that each constant section $a$ maps to the same constant section $a$. Uniqueness among maps with this property follows from the universal property [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]: such a map has prescribed composite with the constant-presheaf unit at every object. This establishes (2) as an isomorphism of rings, including multiplication and identity, without inferring a ring assertion merely from a module-valued assertion.

proof.text: For an $A_X$-module sheaf $F$, [def-pur-localized-ringed-site] gives the sheaf $F|_W$ with its sectionwise $A_X(V)$-module action and sends a sheaf morphism $\varphi$ to its same component $\varphi_V$. Pull this action back along the ring isomorphism of step 3: for $a\in A_W(V)$ and $s\in F(V)$ put $a\cdot s=e_{P,V}(a)s$. For an arrow $T\to V$, the old semilinearity and naturality of $e_P$ give $(e_{P,V}(a)s)|_T=e_{P,V}(a)|_T\,s|_T=e_{P,T}(a|_T)s|_T$, the required restriction identity in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. For example $e_{P,V}(ab)s=e_{P,V}(a)e_{P,V}(b)s$ and $e_{P,V}(1)s=s$ give the associative and unit action laws; the additive laws follow by distributing the ring homomorphism and the old action. A restricted module morphism remains linear; identities and compositions are unchanged componentwise. Using $e_P^{-1}$ reverses the change of ring actions: the two composites act by $e_{P,V}(e_{P,V}^{-1}(b))s=bs$ and $e_{P,V}^{-1}(e_{P,V}(a))s=as$, and leave every underlying morphism unchanged. Combined with the site identification from step 2, these mutually inverse operations identify the two module-sheaf categories and give exactly the restriction functor in (3).

Assume $j$ is an open immersion. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-monomorphism], if $a,b:V\to W$ give the same composite $V\to X$, then $a=b$. Existence of such an $X$-morphism is exactly the factorization equation by definition. If it exists then its underlying point map has image in the open image of $W$. Conversely, if the image of $V\to X$ is contained in that open image, identify $W$ with this open subscheme by [def-weil-open-immersion] and apply [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] to obtain the factorization. Thus existence is equivalent to the asserted set-theoretic condition, and uniqueness has already been proved. Step 1 also ensures that this factorization is an object of $W_{\mathrm{proet}}$. This proves (4).
